Celle d'un conditionnel passé : je t'aur: That of a past conditional: I would have helped you
Celui qui est venu hier est mon frère: The one who came yesterday is my brother
Certaines structures sont calquées sur l: Some structures are calqued on Castilian. “Hi ha” remains invariable, even before a plural. Say “adonar-se” for to notice. To express simultaneity, the careful register prefers “en” + infinitive.
Certains adjectifs changent de sens selo: Some adjectives change meaning depending on the verb. With ser, you describe a permanent quality of the person or thing. With estar, you describe a temporary state or an impression of the moment.
Certains castillanismes très répandus à: Some Castilianisms that are widespread in speech should be avoided in a careful register. Say assabentar-se and not “enterar-se”, aconseguir and not “lograr”, des de and not “desde”, haver de + infinitive and not “tindre que”.
Certains mots ressemblent au français ma: Some words look like French but do not have the same meaning. Estar constipat means to have a cold. Embarassada means pregnant, not embarrassed (for embarrassment, say fer vergonya or estar incòmode). Molestar means to disturb, to bother.
Certains verbes changent de nuance à la: Some verbs change nuance in the pronominal form. Ir means “to go”, irse “to go away, to leave”. Dormir means “to sleep”, dormirse “to fall asleep”. Quedar means “to arrange to meet” or “to remain (there is some left)”, quedarse “to stay somewhere”. Llevar means “to carry, to take (someone)”, llevarse “to take away, to take with you”.
Ces adverbes très galiciens remplacent a: These very Galician adverbs are a good replacement for forms calqued on Spanish. Axiña means “quickly, soon”, decontado “right away”, a miúdo “often” and de cando en vez “from time to time”.
Ces conjonctions de but, d'antériorité,: These conjunctions of purpose, anteriority, limit and manner are always followed by the subjunctive. When possible, Galician often prefers preposition + infinitive, possibly personal.
Ces connecteurs introduisent une opposit: These connectors introduce a contrast (“however, nevertheless, yet”). porén and non obstante belong to a written or formal register, emporiso is very Galician and somewhat literary. They can move within the sentence and are set off by commas.

These connectors introduce a contrast after an accepted fact, like “nevertheless”, “even so” or “for all that”. No obstante is rather written and formal, con todo is formal, aun así is common both in speech and in writing.

These connectors introduce a contrast with what precedes, like “nevertheless”, “however”, “despite everything”. No obstant això and tanmateix belong to careful writing. Així i tot and amb tot stress that the obstacle did not prevent the result. Used alone before a noun, no obstant means “despite”.
Ces connecteurs opposent une idée à la p: These connectors contrast one idea with the previous one (= nevertheless, however, despite everything). “No obstant això” and “tanmateix” are formal, whereas “així i tot” and “tot i així” are more neutral. Used alone, “no obstant” works as a preposition followed by a noun.
Ces deux mots sont des pièges classiques: These two words are classic traps for French speakers.
Ces locutions conditionnelles se constru: These conditional phrases are constructed with the subjunctive: a non ser que (“unless”), sempre que (“provided that”), no caso de que (“in case”). With the indicative, sempre que changes meaning and means “whenever”.
Ces quatre mots touchent au travail mais: These four words relate to work but are not interchangeable. lana is work in general or a task, lanbidea the trade or profession, lanpostua the specific job position, ogibidea the livelihood, the source of income.
Ces tournures expriment une concession i: These expressions express an intensive concession (“however much”, “however... ”). They take the subjunctive when the action is hypothetical. por moito que and por máis que go with a verb, while por moi + adjective or adverb + que refers to a quality.
Ces tournures traduisent « avoir beau »: These expressions translate “however much” or “however…”. With the subjunctive, the fact is presented as hypothetical or unimportant. With the indicative, it refers to a real or habitual fact. Por muy + adjective or adverb + que is almost always constructed with the subjunctive.
Ces verbes s'accordent avec la chose qui: These verbs agree with the thing that pleases or hurts, and the person is expressed by an indirect object pronoun (me, che, lle, nos, vos, lles). If the thing is plural, the verb goes into the plural. At the start of an affirmative sentence, the pronoun is attached after the verb.

Dans l'exclamation, le valencien reprend: In exclamations, Valencian readily repeats the verb with a second que: que + adjective or adverb + que + verb, quin or quina + noun + que + verb. Dans la clivée, l'élément focalisé est à: In the cleft sentence, the focused element is in the absolutive with izan, followed by a nominalised relative clause.
Dans la condition irréelle, imparfait du: In an unreal condition, imperfect subjunctive: fóra (from ser). Never the conditional after si.
Dans la langue juridique et administrati: In legal and administrative language, the future subjunctive is still used in relative and conditional clauses referring to a possible future: quen incumprir, se houber, o que dispuxer. It is formed on the preterite stem (fixen gives fixer, puiden gives puider). In everyday language, it is replaced by the present subjunctive or indicative.
Dans la langue soignée, on trouve aussi: In careful language, the future subjunctive is also found: cando chegares.

Dans les textes juridiques, la relative: In legal texts, a relative clause referring to a possible future uses the future subjunctive.

Dans une hypothèse avec un conditionnel: In a hypothesis with a conditional in the main clause, si is followed by the imperfect subjunctive: tinguéssim.

Dans une phrase irréelle, la forme en -r: In an unreal sentence, the -ra form can have the value of a conditional perfect, in careful language.
Dans une relative, on emploie l'indicati: In a relative clause, the indicative is used when the antecedent is known and exists. The subjunctive is used when looking for something whose existence is unknown, or when denying it (no hay nadie que, no conozco a nadie que). French sometimes makes the same distinction (qui ait), but Spanish applies it systematically.

De manera que + subjonctif exprime le bu: De manera que + subjunctive expresses purpose.
De modo que exprime ici un but et prend: De modo que expresses purpose here and takes the present subjunctive.

De payer un supplément pour obtenir un m: To pay a supplement to get a new model.

De xeito que + subjonctif exprime le but: De xeito que + subjunctive expresses purpose: present subjunctive oian.
De xeito que et de maneira que suivis de: De xeito que and de maneira que followed by the indicative express a consequence (so that, with the result that). Followed by the subjunctive, they express purpose (in such a way that). Así que and polo que also introduce a consequence, always in the indicative.
Deber + infinitif exprime l'obligation m: Deber + infinitive expresses a moral obligation or advice, tener que a concrete obligation, haber que (hay que) an impersonal obligation. Deber de + infinitive expresses a supposition (“he must be…”). In everyday language, deber alone is also used for supposition, but deber de for obligation is considered incorrect.
Deber de + infinitif exprime plutôt une: Deber de + infinitive rather expresses a supposition: debe de ser tarde (it must be late).

Decir que + indicatif transmet une infor: Decir que + indicative passes on information.
Decir que + subjonctif transmet un ordre: Decir que + subjunctive passes on an order.

Deitu se construit avec le datif : amari: Deitu is constructed with the dative: amari deitu diot.
Deixar de + infinitif signifie « cesser: Deixar de + infinitive means “to cease”. Dexei is a spelling mistake.
Deixar signifie aussi prêter dans la lan: Deixar also means to lend in everyday language.
Deixar signifie laisser, mais aussi prêt: Deixar means to leave, but also to lend, especially in everyday language. The verb prestar also exists for “to lend”. The context always makes it possible to tell the two meanings apart.

Dentro de + durée signifie « dans » pour: Dentro de + duration means “in” to situate a future moment. En + duration indicates the time needed to do something (in an hour). A partir de means “from”. Al cabo de means “after”.

Description et habitude au passé : impar: Description and habit in the past: imperfect (era, ía), with ser for age.

Deure + infinitif exprime ici la probabi: Deure + infinitive expresses probability here, and uns trenta means “about thirty”.

Devant arren, la forme conjuguée prend -: Before arren, the conjugated form takes -(e)n: duen arren.
Devant en, et prend sa forme pleine : te: Before en, et takes its full form: te'n.
Devant en, le pronom em prend sa forme p: Before en, the pronoun em takes its full form: me'n.
Devant la conjonction que, ces prépositi: Before the conjunction que, these prepositions disappear: penso que..., estic segur que...
Devant que, la préposition se maintient: Before que, the preposition is kept in careful language: decatarse de que.
Devant un adjectif ou un adverbe, on emp: Before an adjective or an adverb, use tan ... com. Before a noun, tant agrees: tant, tanta, tants, tantes ... com. After a verb, say tant com. The second term is introduced by com, never by que.

Before an adjective or an adverb, use tan... como (as... as). Before a noun, tanto agrees: tanto, tanta, tantos, tantas... como (as much/many... as). After a verb, say tanto como (as much as). In speech, igual de + adjective + que is very common.
Before an adjective or an adverb, use tan... que.
Devant un adjectif, l'égalité s'exprime: Before an adjective, equality is expressed with tan… com.
Devant un adjectif, le comparatif d'égal: Before an adjective, the comparative of equality is tan ... com.
Devant un infinitif, la préposition se m: Before an infinitive, the preposition is generally kept: m'alegro de veure't.
Devant un infinitif, per a exprime le bu: Before an infinitive, per a expresses purpose (for, in order to) and per expresses cause (for, because). The Valencian standard maintains this distinction. With a noun or a pronoun, per a also marks the recipient and the deadline.

Devant un infinitif, per exprime la caus: Before an infinitive, per expresses cause.
Devant un nom masculin singulier : tanto: Before a masculine singular noun: tanto... como.

Devant un nombre, on dit « més de » et «: Before a number, say “més de” and “menys de”.
Devant une consonne, le pronom de 1re pe: Before a consonant, the 1st person pronoun placed before the verb is em.
Devant une consonne, le pronom s'écrit «: Before a consonant, the pronoun is written “es” and not “se”: es venen, es busca.
Devant une durée, « depuis » se dit desd: Before a length of time, “for” is desde hace.

L'espagnol n'a pas un verbe unique pour: Spanish has no single verb for “to become”. Ponerse + adjective indicates a temporary change (mood, appearance, health). Quedarse indicates the result of an event (quedarse sin trabajo, quedarse ciego).
L'euphémisme adoucit une réalité désagré: Euphemism softens an unpleasant reality and is very common in administration and business. Irony often works through antiphrasis or through adjectives placed before the noun such as menudo or valiente, which take on a negative meaning.
L'examen a été reporté d'une semaine : c: The exam has been postponed by a week: that's a bit of breathing space at least.

L'imparfait (imperfet) se forme sur le r: The imperfect (imperfet) is formed on the infinitive stem. Verbs in -ar: -ava, -aves, -ava, -àvem, -àveu, -aven. Verbs in -re, -er and -ir: -ia, -ies, -ia, -íem, -íeu, -ien. The 1st and 2nd persons plural have a written accent.
L'imparfait de beure est irrégulier : be: The imperfect of beure is irregular: bevia, bevies, bevia… without an accent in the singular.
L'imparfait de fer est irrégulier : feia: The imperfect of fer is irregular: feia, feies, feia, fèiem, fèieu, feien.
L'imparfait de ser fait era, eres, era,: The imperfect of ser is era, eres, era, érem, éreu, eren.
L'imparfait du subjonctif des verbes en: The imperfect subjunctive of verbs in -ar and -re/-er is formed with -és, -essis, -és, -éssim, -éssiu, -essin, and that of verbs in -ir with -ís, -issis, -ís, -íssim, -íssiu, -issin. Irregular verbs start from the preterite stem: tingués, vingués, fos, fes. It is used after a main verb in the past or the conditional and in hypotheses introduced by si.
L'imparfait du subjonctif se forme avec: The imperfect subjunctive is formed with the endings -és, -essis, -és, -éssim, -éssiu, -essin (verbs in -ar and -re) and -ís, -issis, -ís, -íssim, -íssiu, -issin (verbs in -ir). It is mainly used after “si” in unreal hypotheses and after a main verb in the past or the conditional.
L'imparfait du subjonctif se forme sur l: The imperfect subjunctive is formed on the preterite (tuvieron) and the 1st person plural always has a written accent.
L'imparfait du subjonctif se forme à par: The imperfect subjunctive is formed from the 3rd person plural of the preterite (tuvieron, hicieron, fueron): remove -ron and add -ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -rais, -ran or -se, -ses, -se, -semos, -seis, -sen. The two series are equivalent, but the -ra form is the most frequent in speech in Spain. The 1st person plural always has a written accent: tuviéramos, fuésemos.
L'imparfait du subjonctif valencien se t: The Valencian imperfect subjunctive ends in -ara (verbs in -ar), -era or -ira, with the persons -ara, -ares, -ara, -àrem, -àreu, -aren. Irregular verbs start from the same stem as the preterite: verbs whose present subjunctive is in -ga form their imperfect in -guera. Thus tindre gives tinguera, vindre vinguera, poder poguera, voler volguera, dir diguera, haver haguera, estar estiguera, conéixer coneguera, beure beguera, viure visquera. Ser gives fóra and fer gives fera.
L'imparfait décrit les habitudes et les: The imperfect describes habits and situations in the past. Verbs in -ar take -ava, -aves, -ava, -àvem, -àveu, -aven. Verbs in -er, -re and -ir take -ia, -ies, -ia, -íem, -íeu, -ien. Watch out for the written accent in the nosaltres and vosaltres forms.
L'imparfait sert à décrire une situation: The imperfect is used to describe a past situation or habit (“I used to do”, “it was”). The periphrastic past (vaig + infinitive) narrates a completed, one-off action (“I did”). In a narrative, the imperfect sets the scene and the periphrastic past moves the story forward.
L'impératif affirmatif : tu, vosaltres,: The affirmative imperative: tu, vosaltres, vosté
L'impératif courant adressé à zu associe: The usual imperative addressed to zu combines the verb stem (often identical to the participle: itxi, ireki) with an imperative auxiliary: ezazu for a transitive verb with a singular object, itzazu for a plural object, zaitez for an intransitive verb, iezadazu for an action done “for me”.
L'impératif de usted reprend le subjonct: The imperative for usted uses the subjunctive: pase.
L'impératif de vosaltres des verbes en -: The vosaltres imperative of -ar verbs ends in -eu.
L'impératif de vosaltres se termine en -: The vosaltres imperative ends in -eu for -ar verbs, without an accent.
L'impératif de vostè emprunte la forme d: The imperative for vostè borrows the subjunctive form: signi.
L'impératif négatif prend le subjonctif: The negative imperative takes the subjunctive: no obris.
L'impératif négatif se construit avec le: The negative imperative is constructed with the subjunctive: no vingues.
L'impératif rapporté au passé devient im: An imperative reported in the past becomes an imperfect subjunctive in -se.
L'impératif rapporté au passé devient qu: An imperative reported in the past becomes que + imperfect subjunctive: tancara.
L'infinitif personnel se forme sur l'inf: The personal infinitive is formed on the infinitive + -ren. Dixeren is a future subjunctive.
L'infinitif personnel se forme toujours: The personal infinitive is always formed on the infinitive: dicires. Dixeres is a future subjunctive.
L'irréel du passé exige si + plus-que-pa: The past unreal condition requires si + pluperfect subjunctive, never the conditional.
L'irréel du passé se construit avec si +: The past unreal condition is constructed with si + pluperfect subjunctive: hagués sabut.
L'obligation s'exprime avec haver de, pa: Obligation is expressed with haver de, not with the Castilianism tenir que.
L'obligation se dit haver de + infinitif: Obligation is haver de + infinitive. Tindre que is a Castilianism.
L'offre consiste en une remise: The offer consists of a discount
L'oisiveté pousse à s'occuper de futilit: Idleness leads people to busy themselves with trivialities
L'ordre est toujours es + pronom de pers: The order is always es + personal pronoun: “me s'ha trencat” is incorrect.
L'orthographe est la même pour toutes le: The spelling is the same for all varieties.
L'université va lancer un programme de b: The university is going to launch a grant programme.
L'utilisation du téléphone portable avan: Using a mobile phone before going to bed.
The deadline is expressed with per a.
L'écrit académique galicien dispose de f: Galician academic writing has its own formulas: cómpre (“it is necessary, it is advisable”) + infinitive, salientar (“to highlight”), no que atinxe a or no tocante a (“regarding”), á luz de (“in the light of”). They give the text a formal, idiomatic register.

La correspondance administrative utilise: Administrative correspondence uses fixed formulas, the formal form of address (usted) and impersonal constructions. These formulas are not used in everyday speech.

La forme avec le pronom devant vaig est: The form with the pronoun before vaig is the most frequent in speech.
La forme correcte est primavera. Les tro: The correct form is primavera. The other three words are correct.
La forme en -ra est correcte dans les de: The -ra form is correct in both parts of the unreal sentence (se mo dixeras, axudárate), with a literary nuance.

La jubilación est la retraite (jubilarse: La jubilación is retirement (jubilarse, to retire). La competencia often means competition (between companies). Un cargo is a post, a position. La plantilla is the workforce, all the staff. La dirección means management, but also address.
La lecture lente n'a plus sa place aujou: Slow reading no longer has a place today
La lettre ? Je la lui envoie aujourd'hui: The letter? I'm sending it to him today

La lettre formelle commence par « Benvol: A formal letter begins with “Benvolgut senyor” or “Benvolguda senyora” followed by a comma. The formal form of address is “vostè” or, in administration, “vós” with the 2nd person plural. It ends with “Atentament” or “Cordialment”, followed by the signature.

La loi a été approuvée par le Parlement: The law was passed by Parliament

La particule omen, placée juste devant l: The particle omen, placed just before the auxiliary or the conjugated verb, indicates that the information is reported: “apparently, so they say”. It often corresponds to the journalistic conditional in French.
The particle omen, placed just before the conjugated verb, indicates that you are reporting information you have heard, without vouching for it. In the negative, it follows ez: ez omen da etorriko.
La particule ote, placée devant le verbe: The particle ote, placed before the conjugated verb, adds a nuance of doubt or puzzlement to a question (“I wonder”). It is also found in indirect questions: ez dakit etorriko ote den.
La passive avec ser + participe accordé: The passive with ser + agreeing participle (and possibly per + agent) belongs mainly to the written, administrative and journalistic register. The participle of ser is sigut (or estat). When the agent is not expressed, the reflexive passive is generally more natural.
La passive périphrastique se forme avec: The periphrastic passive is formed with ser + participle agreeing with the subject, and the agent is introduced by per. It is mainly common in the press and formal texts. In speech, the pronominal passive or the active sentence is preferred.
La personne avec qui j'ai parlé était tr: The person I spoke to was very kind

La presse emploie des marqueurs de dista: The press uses distancing markers for unverified information: presunto (alleged), al parecer, según fuentes… The “rumour” conditional (habría confesado) is very widespread in the media, but style guides recommend other constructions instead.
La proposition est intéressante. Toutefo: The proposal is interesting. However, it's too expensive
La propriété de la maison appartient aux: The house is owned by the two brothers
La préposition de disparaît devant la co: The preposition de disappears before the conjunction que: m'alegre que.

La pêche était le principal gagne-pain d: Fishing was the village's main livelihood
The question caught me off guard.
La relative au subjonctif: The relative clause in the subjunctive
The relative clause in -(e)n comes before the noun.
La relative en -(e)n se place avant le n: The relative clause in -(e)n goes before the noun, with no relative pronoun: the function of the noun (subject, object, place) is deduced from the auxiliary and the context. The noun then takes the case required by the main clause.
La répétition s'exprime avec tornar a +: Repetition is expressed with tornar a + infinitive.
La réunion a été convoquée à la demande: The meeting was called at the request of local residents.
La semaine dernière ils ont fermé le mag: Last week they closed the shop
La structure lo + adjectif ou adverbe +: The structure lo + adjective or adverb + que + verb expresses intensity, like “how” in English. Despite lo, the adjective agrees with the noun it refers to. It often follows verbs such as no sabes, me sorprende or ya verás.
La technologie a surtout compliqué notre: Technology has mainly complicated our daily lives
La tournure haver-hi (il y a) se conjugu: The construction haver-hi (there is) is conjugated in all tenses in the third person: hi havia, hi va haver, hi haurà, hi hauria, que hi haja, si hi haguera. The pronoun hi is compulsory. The standard recommends the singular even before a plural noun.
La vie en ville lui semblait un paradis,: City life seemed like paradise to him, but from afar everything looks better.
La voiture ? Je te la prête à condition: The car? I'll lend it to you provided you give it back to me on Saturday
La voiture, je l'ai vendue l'an dernier: The car, I sold it last year
Let him do it, he has the knack.
Laisser la mairie garantir seule l'équil: To let the town hall alone guarantee the balance between shops
Laura is a feminine singular direct object: la.
Le -de se maintient devant vos et le mot: The -de is kept before vos and the word, stressed on the antepenultimate syllable, takes an accent.
Le 15, c'est-à-dire vendredi, nous avons: On the 15th, that is to say Friday, we have a meeting.
Le Batua admet souvent deux mots, l'un p: Batua often allows two words, one rather western, the other rather eastern (Navarre, Iparralde). Both are correct: ondo / ongi (well), ume / haur (child), esan / erran (to say), hitz egin / mintzatu (to speak), pasatu / iragan (to pass).
Le but : perquè, per tal que, a fi que: Purpose: perquè, per tal que, a fi que
Le c de pouco devient qu devant i : pouq: The c of pouco becomes qu before i: pouquiño.
Le cas échéant, nous vous ferons parveni: Where appropriate, we will send you the documents by registered post.
Le castillan « por mucho que » fonctionn: Castilian “por mucho que” works in the same way.
Le catalan central utilise les formes en: Central Catalan uses the forms in -és (tingués, vingués, fos). In Valencian, the form in -ara/-era is the most common. In the 1st and 2nd persons plural, the accent is acute: tinguérem, tinguéreu.
Le catalan occidental distingue a et e a: Western Catalan distinguishes unstressed a and e ; Eastern Catalan reduces them to [ə].
Le catalan oriental (central, baléare) r: Eastern Catalan (Central, Balearic) reduces unstressed a and e to a neutral sound [ə] and pronounces unstressed o as [u]. Western Catalan (Lleida, Andorra, Valencian) distinguishes unstressed a and e and generally pronounces unstressed o as [o]. This is the most audible feature between the two main dialect blocks.
Le catalan utilise de nombreuses périphr: Catalan uses many periphrases: estar a punt de (to be about to), posar-se a (to start to), deixar de (to stop), anar + gerund (progression), soler + infinitive (habit). Deure + infinitive mainly expresses probability or supposition, whereas obligation is preferably expressed with haver de.
Le collègue dont je t'ai parlé: The colleague I told you about
Le comparatif de supériorité se construi: The comparative of superiority is constructed with més… que.
Le complément direct (COD) se remplace p: The direct object is replaced by lo, la, los, las according to gender and number: it is the thing or person you see, buy, know. The indirect object, introduced by a (to someone), is replaced by le or les, with no gender distinction. The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb. Tip: when English says “to him”, “to her” or “to them”, it's le or les.
Le complément du superlatif est introdui: The complement of the superlative is introduced by de, here contracted to da.
Le complément du superlatif se construit: The complement of the superlative is constructed with de, and de + el contracts to del.
Le complément indirect détaché (a la dir: The dislocated indirect object (a la directora) is picked up by li.
Le conditionnel adoucit une demande ou u: The conditional softens a request or a wish and is used to give advice. It is formed on the infinitive + -ía, -ías, -ía, -iamos, -iades, -ían. The 1st and 2nd persons plural are written without an accent.
Le conditionnel agrairíem s'accorde avec: The conditional agrairíem agrees with the imperfect subjunctive remetera.
Le conditionnel composé se forme avec ha: The conditional perfect is formed with haber in the conditional + invariable participle (habería feito, haberiamos dito). It expresses a past action that did not happen or a supposition about the past. It is less frequent than in French: the simple conditional or the -ra form is often preferred when the context is sufficient. Do not use ter + participle, which in Galician expresses repetition.
The conditional perfect is formed with hauria + participle.

The conditional perfect is formed with hauria, hauries, hauria, hauríem, hauríeu, haurien + participle. It expresses an action that could have happened in the past, a reproach or a regret. In the main clause of a past unreal sentence, the standard also allows the pluperfect subjunctive (hagués + participle).
Le conditionnel de poder adoucit la dema: The conditional of poder softens the request.
Le conditionnel de voler est voldria, av: The conditional of voler is voldria, with a d.
Le conditionnel deuria exprime le consei: The conditional deuria expresses advice. Hauries would require de (hauries de descansar).
The conditional is impossible after si. In the main clause, habría and hubiera are both correct.
Le conditionnel passé (habría, habrías,: The conditional perfect (habría, habrías, habría… + participle) expresses an action that did not happen: regret, reproach or advice after the event. In reported speech, it also expresses a completed future action seen from the past. For “I should have”, the simple conditional of deber or tener que followed by a perfect infinitive is preferred.
Le conditionnel passé se forme avec le c: The conditional perfect is formed with the conditional of haver (hauria, hauries, hauria, hauríem, hauríeu, haurien) and the participle. It is used to express regret, reproach or a possibility that did not materialise. “I should have” is hauria hagut de, “I could have” hauria pogut.
Le conditionnel se forme sur l'infinitif: The conditional is formed on the infinitive + -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían. The irregular verbs are the same as in the future: tendría, haría, diría, podría, saldría. It is used to ask politely, to express a wish and to give advice. Yo que tú + conditional means “if I were you”.

The conditional is formed on the infinitive with the endings -ia, -ies, -ia, -íem, -íeu, -ien. It expresses politeness, wishes, advice and hypotheses. Irregular verbs have the same stem as in the future: faria, tindria, vindria, podria, voldria, sabria, hauria.
Le conditionnel se forme sur la même bas: The conditional is formed on the same base as the future with the endings -ia, -ies, -ia, -íem, -íeu, -ien. It is used to express politeness, wishes, advice and the consequence of a hypothesis.
Le conseil a décidé de reporter l'assemb: The board decided to postpone the meeting
Le conseil s'exprime au conditionnel : d: Advice is expressed in the conditional: deberías.
Le courrier formel valencien suit des fo: Formal Valencian correspondence follows fixed formulas. You begin with Benvolgut senyor or Benvolguda senyora, use the formal vosté, phrase requests in the conditional followed by the imperfect subjunctive (li agrairíem que…) and finish with Atentament.
Le destinatif -rako indique aussi une éc: The destinative -rako also indicates a deadline (“for, by”) and purpose in the question zertarako (what for).
Le dimanche, il faut toujours faire la q: On Sundays, you always have to queue at the bakery.
Le diminutif galicien est -iño/-iña (-ci: The Galician diminutive is -iño/-iña (-ciño after -n or a stressed vowel), often more affectionate than about size. Augmentatives take -ón/-ona, the colloquial pejorative -ote. The ending -ito is a Castilianism. Some derivatives are lexicalised and have their own meaning, such as cadeirón (armchair).
Le diminutif galicien est -iño/-iña. -it: The Galician diminutive is -iño/-iña. -ito is a Castilianism.
The deadline is extended until tomorrow.
Le délai est écoulé. Par conséquent, auc: The deadline has passed. Consequently, no further applications will be accepted.
Le délai se dit « termini » ; « plaç » e: The deadline is “termini” ; “plaç” is a Castilianism.
Le délai sera automatiquement prolongé d: The deadline will automatically be extended by ten days
Le détenu aurait avoué le vol (informati: The detainee is said to have confessed to the theft (unconfirmed information).
The detainee should have confessed to the theft.
The detainee will confess to the theft.
Le film dont je t'ai parlé: The film I told you about
Le film est sur le point de commencer: The film is about to start
Le français dit « comme s'il était » à l: French says “comme s'il était” in the indicative, hence the frequent mistake como si era.
Le français fonctionne de la même façon,: French works the same way, but Catalan uses the subjunctive more consistently.
Le français met toujours le subjonctif a: French always uses the subjunctive after “bien que”, which is not the case in Valencian.
Le français « devenir » se rend par plus: “To become” is rendered by several verbs. Esdevenir is formal and general. Fer-se is used for age, profession or a gradual change (fer-se gran). Tornar-se indicates a change of character, posar-se a temporary state, quedar-se the result of a loss.
Le français « venir de + infinitif » se: “To have just + participle” (French “venir de + infinitive”) is translated by acabar de + infinitive, never by vindre de. Tornar a + infinitive expresses repetition (re-, again). Deixar de + infinitive means to stop. Estar a punt de + infinitive means to be about to.
Le futur antérieur (habrá salido) exprim: The future perfect (habrá salido) expresses a supposition about a recent past event, linked to the present. The conditional (sería, estaría) expresses a supposition about a moment in the past. English uses “must have” or “must have been”.
Le futur antérieur exprime une suppositi: The future perfect expresses a supposition about a past event linked to the present.
Le futur de pór (poñer) se forme sur por: The future of pór (poñer) is formed on por-: porei.
Le futur devient conditionnel, et demà d: The future becomes conditional, and demà becomes l'endemà.
Le futur du subjonctif (cantar, cantares: The future subjunctive (cantar, cantares, cantar, cantarmos, cantardes, cantaren) is formed on the preterite stem for irregular verbs: fixer, dixer, tiver, souber, quixer, puider, for. In everyday language, it survives mainly in set phrases and after quen, o que, como, cando with a hypothetical value. It remains frequent in legal and administrative texts, and the present subjunctive often replaces it in conversation.
Le futur du subjonctif des irréguliers s: The future subjunctive of irregular verbs is formed on the preterite stem (fixen): fixeres. Faceres is the personal infinitive.
Le futur du subjonctif se forme sur le r: The future subjunctive is formed on the preterite stem (houbo): houber.
Le futur exprime une supposition sur le: The future expresses a supposition about the present.
Le futur peut exprimer une supposition s: The future can express a supposition about the present, and the conditional a supposition about the past. It is the equivalent of English “it must be…” or “it must have been…”.
Le futur se forme en ajoutant à l'infini: The future is formed by adding the endings -é, -às, -à, -em, -eu, -an to the infinitive (verbs in -re lose the final e: beure gives beuré). It expresses a future action, but also a probability in the present.
Le futur se forme sur l'infinitif avec l: The future is formed on the infinitive with the endings -é, -às, -à, -em, -eu, -an. Verbs in -re lose the final e: beure gives beuré, viure gives viuré. The main irregular verbs are faré, tindré, vindré, podré, voldré, sabré, hauré, aniré.
Le futur simple exprime une supposition: The simple future expresses a supposition about the present.
Le futur simple sert à exprimer une prob: The simple future is used to express a probability or a supposition about the present, where English says “must” or “probably”. It does not refer to the future. In questions, it translates “I wonder”.
Le galicien dit liberdade, avec le suffi: Galician says liberdade, with the suffix -dade.
Le galicien emploie o, a, os, as pour le: Galician uses o, a, os, as for the direct object, even for a person: chameino (I called him), not chameille, which imitates Castilian leísmo. Lle is reserved for the indirect object. Likewise, the Castilian construction ir a por is wrong: say ir por (contracted to polo, pola) or ir buscar.
Le galicien emploie un pronom che (vos p: Galician uses a pronoun che (vos for several people) with no grammatical function at all: it involves the listener emotionally and makes the sentence livelier. Very frequent in speech, it is typical of Galician. It is not translated, except sometimes by “you know” or “I tell you”.
Le galicien n'a pas de passé composé : l: Galician has no present perfect: the preterite also translates “I have done”.
Le galicien parlé insère souvent un pron: Spoken Galician often inserts a dative pronoun with no grammatical function, the dativo de solidariedade: che for someone you address as tu, lle for someone you address formally, vos in the plural. It involves the listener and gives an expressive, warm tone. It is not translated, except by “you know” or “you see”.
Le galicien peut ajouter un pronom che (: Galician can add a pronoun che (ti) or vos (vós) that plays no grammatical role: it involves the listener and gives an affectionate or expressive tone. It is not translated word for word. It is mainly used in speech, with people you address informally.
Le galicien renforce une affirmation ave: Galician reinforces a statement with si que (“really, this time”), with abofé or abofé que (“certainly”, somewhat literary) or with ben placed before the verb (“well”). These intensifiers are very frequent in speech and add emphasis.
Le garçon qui travaille avec moi est de: The boy who works with me is from Cádiz
The demonym for Alcoi is alcoià, alcoiana.
Le gentilé de Gandia est gandià, gandian: The demonym for Gandia is gandià, gandiana.
Le grand-père a fini son travail en mars: Grandad finished his work in March.
Le gérondif (cantant, venint) exprime un: The gerund (cantant, venint) expresses a simultaneous or immediately prior action, manner, cause or condition. It must not express a subsequent action or be used as an adjective after a noun: use a coordination with i or a relative clause instead. Pronouns go after the gerund.
Le gérondif : emplois corrects et incorr: The gerund: correct and incorrect uses
Le gérondif composé havent + participe m: The perfect gerund havent + participle marks anteriority.
Le gérondif exprime ici la manière (simu: Here the gerund expresses manner (simultaneity). It can neither be used as an adjective nor express a subsequent action.
Le gérondif exprime la simultanéité, la: The gerund expresses simultaneity, manner, cause or condition. The perfect gerund (havent + participle) marks anteriority. It must not express a subsequent action, or be used as an adjective before a complement: use a coordination or a relative clause instead.
Le gérondif ne s'emploie pas comme adjec: The gerund is not used as an adjective: use a relative clause.
Le jour où je suis arrivé, il pleuvait: The day I arrived, it was raining
Le juge rendra son jugement demain: The judge will deliver his judgment tomorrow
Le juge rendra son jugement la semaine p: The judge will deliver his judgment next week
Le langage juridique et administratif re: Legal and administrative language relies on fixed collocations that must be learnt as a whole: interposar un recurs, dictar sentència, presentar al·legacions, el termini venç. The verb cannot be replaced by an everyday synonym: you don't say “posar un recurs”.
Le leísmo de chose ou de personne fémini: Leísmo for things or for feminine persons is not accepted.
Le livre ? Je le lui rendrai demain: The book? I'll give it back to him tomorrow
Le livre que tu m'as prêté est génial: The book you lent me is great
Le livre que tu m'as prêté est très inté: The book you lent me is very interesting.
Le logement est de plus en plus cher: Housing is getting more and more expensive
Le loyer au centre coûte les yeux de la: Rent in the centre costs an arm and a leg.
Le loyer est de sept cents euros, charge: The rent is seven hundred euros, including service charges.
Le mode du verbe après perquè change com: The mood of the verb after perquè completely changes the meaning of the sentence.
Next month, I'm going to move house.
Le médecin m'a dit que je devais me repo: The doctor told me I had to rest for a few days.
Le nom de famille se dit apellido. En Es: Surname is apellido. In Spain, everyone has two: the father's and the mother's.
Le nom est singulier, donc le verbe auss: The noun is singular, so the verb is too, and the pronoun is written es before a consonant.
Le nom verbal + -ko exprime le but quand: Verbal noun + -ko expresses purpose when the subject is the same or general (“to + infinitive”). It is also used as a noun complement: “something to do, the time to do”.
Le nom verbal -tzea sert d'infinitif suj: The verbal noun -tzea is used as a subject infinitive.
Le nom verbal en -t(z)e se décline comme: The verbal noun in -t(z)e is declined like a noun: -t(z)ea (subject or object), -t(z)eaz (of, about), -t(z)eagatik (for, because of). It is often equivalent to an English infinitive or -ing form.
Le nom verbal en -tzea ou -tea (même bas: The verbal noun in -tzea or -tea (same base as the habitual: erretzen, erretzea) is used as a subject or object infinitive. It is declined: subject of a transitive verb in the ergative (hitz egiteak), object in the absolutive.
Le nom verbal suivi de -ko (-tzeko, -tek: The verbal noun followed by -ko (-tzeko, -teko) expresses purpose (“to, in order to”) or what a thing is for (“to drink, to do”). It goes before the main verb or after the noun it qualifies.
Le nom verbal à l'inessif (-tzean, -tean: The verbal noun in the inessive (-tzean, -tean) indicates the moment when the main action takes place: “on arriving, when going out”. The form does not change with tense or person.
Le non-respect de ces conditions entraîn: Failure to comply with these conditions will result in the immediate cancellation of the booking.
Le notaire a certifié la signature du co: The notary certified the signing of the contract.
Le notaire atteste que le document est a: The notary attests that the document is authentic.
Le pain ? C'est moi qui l'achète: The bread? I'm the one who buys it
Le paquet ? Je le lui apporte demain: The parcel? I'll bring it to him tomorrow
Le participe de construir prend un tréma: The participle of construir takes a diaeresis and agrees here with the masculine pont.
Le participe de ser est sigut, invariabl: The participle of ser is sigut, invariable after haver.
Le participe suivi de l'instrumental -z: The participle followed by the instrumental -z (-ez after a consonant) expresses manner or means, like the English “by … -ing”: irakurriz, entzunez, eginez.
Le passif avec ser + participe accordé (: The passive with ser + agreeing participle (foi aprobada) belongs mainly to the press and formal writing, and the agent is introduced by por, contracted with the article (polo, pola). In everyday language, the reflexive passive (aprobouse a lei) is preferred, in which the verb agrees with the grammatical subject and the agent is not expressed. The pronoun se follows the usual rules of enclisis and proclisis.
Le passif se forme avec ser + participe: The passive is formed with ser + participle agreeing in gender and number with the subject, the agent being introduced by por. It belongs mainly to the written language (press, official texts, history). In speech, Spanish prefers the active voice or the pasiva refleja with se.
Le passé composé de ser se forme avec le: The present perfect of ser is formed with the participle estat: ha estat aprovada.
Le passé composé rapporté au passé devie: A present perfect reported in the past becomes a pluperfect indicative: havia perdut.
Le passé composé s'emploie aussi pour un: The present perfect is also used for an undated experience: ja has estat a Roma?
Le passé simple (pretérito) présente une: The preterite (pretérito) presents a completed, one-off action that moves the narrative forward. The imperfect (copretérito) describes the setting, a habit or an action in progress in the past. In a narrative, the imperfect sets the scene and the preterite tells the event.
Le passé synthétique de joan signifie «: The synthetic past of joan means “I was going, I was on my way”: nindoan, zindoazen, zihoan, gindoazen, zindoazten, zihoazen. It describes movement in progress in the past, often as the backdrop to another event.
Le plan est bon. Cependant, il demande t: The plan is good. However, it requires too much money.
Le pluriel de « paraigua » est « paraigü: The plural of “paraigua” is “paraigües”, with a diaeresis to keep the [gw] sound.
Le plus-que-parfait du subjonctif se for: The pluperfect subjunctive is formed with hagués, haguessis, hagués, haguéssim, haguéssiu, haguessin + participle. After si, it expresses a condition that was not fulfilled in the past, where English uses the past perfect. The main clause then goes into the conditional perfect.

The pluperfect subjunctive is formed with the imperfect subjunctive of haver (haguera, hagueres, haguera, haguérem, haguéreu, hagueren) followed by the participle. It expresses a prior action in a subjunctive subordinate clause when the context is past, the past unreal condition after si, and regret after tant de bo.
Le plus-que-parfait exprime une action a: The pluperfect expresses an action prior to another past action. It is formed with the imperfect of haber (había, habías, había, habíamos, habíais, habían) + invariable participle. Unlike French, the auxiliary is always haber, even for verbs of motion: habíamos salido (we had gone out).
Le poisson du jour était trop salé: The fish of the day was too salty
Le policier municipal lui a mis une amen: The local police officer fined him for obstructive parking.
Le potentiel se construit sur le radical: The potential is built on the stem: sar naiteke.
Le premier constate un fait réel, le sec: The first states a real fact, the second considers a hypothesis
Le premier envisage une hypothèse, le se: The first considers a hypothesis, the second states a real fact
Le premier est au passé, le second au pr: The first is in the past, the second in the present
Le prix a augmenté ; néanmoins, les vent: The price went up ; nevertheless, sales held steady.
Le prix, c'est une chose ; les délais, c: The price is one thing ; the deadlines are a different kettle of fish.
Le professeur a fermé les yeux et ne l'a: The teacher turned a blind eye and didn't punish him.
Le projet a été approuvé par la mairie l: The project was approved by the town hall last week.
Le projet est cher. D'un autre côté, il: The project is expensive. On the other hand, it would open up new markets for us.
Le projet est coûteux. Cependant, il est: The project is costly. However, it is necessary.
Le projet ne verra le jour que si le bud: The project will only see the light of day if the budget allows, which is far from guaranteed.
Le pronom s'écrit soudé au verbe sans tr: The pronoun is written joined to the verb without a hyphen, and the verb agrees with orzamento (singular).
Le pronom se place devant vaig ou après: The pronoun goes before vaig or after the infinitive in the form -me (vaig llevar-me).
The prefix in- becomes im- before p.
Le quartier où j'habite est calme: The neighbourhood where I live is quiet
Le rapport est incomplet et, par conséqu: The report is incomplete and, consequently, it cannot be approved
Le rapport est très complet. Néanmoins,: The report is very thorough. Nevertheless, it contains a few mistakes
Le regret sur le passé avec tant de bo s: Regret about the past with tant de bo is constructed with the pluperfect subjunctive.
Le relatif composé el qual, la qual: The compound relative el qual, la qual
Le relatif sujet sans préposition est qu: The subject relative without a preposition is que ; the verb is in the subjunctive in the 3rd person.
Le reproche sur le passé se construit av: Reproach about the past is constructed with deberías + perfect infinitive (haber + participle).
Le restaurant n'est pas terrible, mais l: The restaurant isn't great, but the price is fair.
Le samedi, je fais les courses au marché: On Saturdays, I do my shopping at the market.
Le se impersonnel s'emploie aussi avec l: Impersonal se is also used with intransitive verbs: En España se cena tarde.
Le souhait poli s'exprime au conditionne: A polite wish is expressed in the conditional: agradaria.
Le subjonctif après la volonté et les se: The subjunctive after will and feelings
Le subjonctif avec perquè, abans que et: The subjunctive with perquè, abans que and sense que
Le subjonctif de saber est irrégulier :: The subjunctive of saber is irregular: sàpia, sàpies, sàpia…
Le subjonctif présent d'eixir est isca,: The present subjunctive of eixir is isca, isques, isca…
Le subjonctif présent de fer est faça, f: The present subjunctive of fer is faça, faces, faça…
Le subjonctif se forme sur conozco : con: The subjunctive is formed on conozco: conozca, conozcas.
Le suffixe -(e)larik s'ajoute à la forme: The suffix -(e)larik is added to the conjugated form (zegoelarik, nintzelarik) and expresses a simultaneous circumstance: “while, whereas, given that”. It belongs mainly to the written, formal language.
Le suffixe -ada est très productif. Il i: The suffix -ada is very productive. It indicates the contents of an object (a spoonful), a blow given with an object, a large quantity or a communal meal centred on a product.
Le suffixe -ada indique le contenu : « c: The suffix -ada indicates the contents: “cullerada”. “Cullereta” is a teaspoon, “cullerot” a ladle.
Le suffixe -dor, -dora désigne l'agent d: The suffix -dor, -dora refers to the agent of an action, an instrument or a machine, or a place. The meaning is not always predictable: each word must be learnt.
Le suffixe -ezin, ajouté au radical verb: The suffix -ezin, added to the verb stem, means “which cannot be …”: sinestezin (unbelievable), ulertezin (incomprehensible), jasanezin (unbearable), ahaztezin (unforgettable). The suffix -gaitz means “difficult to …”: ulergaitz, sinesgaitz. These adjectives take the article like the others.
Le suffixe -garri, ajouté au radical ver: The suffix -garri, added to the verb stem, first indicates what causes an effect (harrigarri, astonishing). But it also expresses what can or deserves to undergo the action: jangarri (edible), edangarri (drinkable), sinesgarri (credible), ikusgarri (worth seeing, spectacular). The stem loses its verbal ending: sinetsi gives sines-garri.
Le suffixe -ment forme le nom d'action :: The suffix -ment forms the action noun: el desenvolupament. “Desarroll” is a Castilianism.
Le suffixe -tud de l'espagnol correspond: The Spanish suffix -tud corresponds to -tude in Galician.
Le suffixe -tzat signifie « pour, en tan: The suffix -tzat means “as, for” with verbs of judgement: hartu, jo, eman. It is added to the indefinite form.
Le suffixe est -íssim avec un accent ; l: The suffix is -íssim with an accent ; the accent of fàcil disappears.
Le sujet dont nous parlions: The subject we were talking about
Le superlatif absolu se forme avec -íssi: The absolute superlative is formed with -íssim, written with ss and an acute accent.
Le superlatif relatif se forme avec arti: The relative superlative is formed with article + noun + més + adjective, without repeating the article as in French. The complement is introduced by de. The absolute superlative is formed with molt + adjective or with the suffix -íssim, -íssima.
Le superlatif relatif se forme avec l'ar: The relative superlative is formed with the article + més or menys (el més car, la menys cara). The absolute superlative is formed with molt or with the suffix -íssim, -íssima (caríssim, boníssima). Before the suffix, the adjective loses its unstressed final vowel and its written accent (fàcil, facilíssim).
Le superlatif relatif se forme avec o, a: The relative superlative is formed with o, a, os, as + máis + adjective, and the complement is introduced by de (contracted with the article if necessary). The absolute superlative is formed with moi + adjective or with the suffix -ísimo. Bo and malo have their own forms: o mellor, o peor.
Le superlatif se forme avec l'article +: The superlative is formed with the article + (noun) + más or menos + adjective + de. Unlike French, the article is not repeated after the noun: la calle más bonita, not la calle la más bonita. The complement is constructed with de (in the neighbourhood, in the city). Mejor and peor go before the noun: el mejor restaurante.
Le temps est très changeant sur la côte: The weather is very changeable on the coast
Le temps se déduit de la principale : le: The tense is deduced from the main clause: the participle does not change.
Le train avait du retard. C'est pourquoi: The train was late. That's why I didn't arrive on time.
Le train encore en retard ? Rien de nouv: The train late again? Nothing new there!
Le train est sur le point de partir: The train is about to leave
The train is about to leave.
Le train part dans dix minutes: The train leaves in ten minutes
Le trait d'union évite que le s entre vo: The hyphen prevents the s between vowels from being pronounced [z].
Le valencien comprend plusieurs variétés: Valencian includes several varieties: northern (north of Castelló), central or apitxat (Valencia and its surroundings), southern (la Safor, l'Alcoià…) and alacantí. Apitxat is recognisable by the devoicing of sibilants and affricates: no distinction between [z] and [s], or between [dʒ] and [tʃ]. These pronunciations are normal in speech, but the spelling remains common to all.
Le valencien forme les noms abstraits pa: Valencian forms abstract nouns by suffixation: -ment and -ció from verbs, -itat and -esa from adjectives, -atge for certain technical actions. The prefix des- marks the opposite, re- repetition. Adjectives in -ble give nouns in -bilitat.
Le valencien forme tous les temps compos: Valencian forms all compound tenses with haver: hauria vingut.
Le valencien n'a pas d'équivalent unique: Valencian has no single equivalent of French “dont” (whose, of which). Depending on the case, de què (for a thing), de qui (for a person) or del qual, de la qual, dels quals, de les quals are used. For possession, del qual or de la qual goes after the possessed noun.
Le valencien possède des adverbes de tem: Valencian has some time adverbs that are very common in speech. Despús-ahir means the day before yesterday and despús-demà the day after tomorrow. Enguany means this year.
Le vendredi, nous faisons la tournée des: On Fridays, we go bar-hopping in the old town.
Le verbe egon (être quelque part, être d: The verb egon (to be somewhere, to be in a state) has a synthetic past: nengoen, zeunden, zegoen, geunden, zeundeten, zeuden. It translates “I was, you were…” for a place or a temporary state.
Le verbe esperar signifie à la fois « at: The verb esperar means both “to wait” and “to hope”. The context lets you choose. “Esperar que” in the sense of “to hope” is followed by the subjunctive. Careful, “atendre” means “to look after, to pay attention”, not “to wait”.
Le verbe est pronominal (alçar-se) et em: The verb is pronominal (alçar-se) and em is elided to m' before a vowel.
The verb fixar-se is constructed with en.
Le verbe galicien est ditar, sans c. dic: The Galician verb is ditar, without a c. dictou is a Castilianism.
Le verbe principal est au passé : la sub: The main verb is in the past: the subordinate clause goes into the imperfect subjunctive.
Le verbe s'accorde avec os pés (pluriel): The verb agrees with os pés (plural), the pronoun is attached and the word, stressed on the antepenultimate syllable, takes an accent.
Le verbe ser à la 1re personne s'écrit s: The verb ser in the 1st person is written soc, without an accent since the 2016 reform (old spelling: sóc).
Le vocabulaire juridico-administratif ga: Galician legal and administrative vocabulary has its own forms, different from Spanish: o prazo (the deadline), o xulgado (the court), o prego de condicións (the specifications), a sentenza (the judgment), o/a demandante and o/a demandado/a. The key verbs are cumprir, incumprir, recorrer and ditar (to deliver a decision).
Le vocatif home et le datif de solidarit: The vocative home and the dative of solidarity che are typical of informal speech.
Le voisin a formé un recours contre l'am: The neighbour lodged an appeal against the fine.
Le voisin du troisième est bon comme le: The neighbour on the third floor is as good as gold.
Le vol a été annulé à cause du brouillar: The flight was cancelled because of the fog
Le week-end, je fais du vélo et je nage: At the weekend, I go cycling and swim at the pool.
Le « rebedor » est la pièce d'entrée où: The “rebedor” is the entrance room where visitors are received.
Lembrar est transitif ; la forme pronomi: Lembrar is transitive ; the pronominal form requires contracted de (daquel).

Les compléments introduits par de se rem: Complements introduced by de are replaced by en. Those introduced by a, en or amb are replaced by hi, unless they are a dative (li, els). So you need to know the preposition governed by the Catalan verb, which does not always match French.
Les composés formés d'un verbe et d'un n: Compounds made of a verb and a noun are written as one word. If they end in -s, they are invariable. If the second element begins with s, r or x after a vowel, a hyphen is used to keep the pronunciation.

Les pronoms compléments d'objet direct d: The 3rd person direct object pronouns are o, a, os, as. Like the other unstressed pronouns, they are attached after the verb in a simple affirmative sentence. After non, xa or a question word, they move before the verb.
Les préfixes des-, in- (im- devant p ou: The prefixes des-, in- (im- before p or b), re-, pre-, sobre- and contra- modify the meaning. The suffixes -miento and -ción form action nouns, -ble adjectives of possibility, -izar verbs.
Les prépositions de concession (malia, a: Prepositions of concession (malia, a pesar de) and cause (por, ao) readily take the personal infinitive, especially when the subject is explicit or different from that of the main verb. Les relatifs français « qui » et « que »: The relatives “who” and “that/which” are both translated by que after a noun: el chico que viene (not el chico quien viene).

Les verbes en -ar font -àvem à nosaltres: Verbs in -ar take -àvem for nosaltres, with a grave accent and a v.

On part de la 1re personne du présent (y: Start from the 1st person of the present (yo), remove the final -o and change the vowel: -ar verbs take -e, -er and -ir verbs take -a. On rapporte une affirmation avec -(e)la: A statement is reported with -(e)la and a question with -(e)n, often preceded by ea. If the introductory verb is in the past, the reported form also shifts to the past (dago becomes zegoela).

Oxalá (pourvu que) est toujours suivi du: Oxalá (I hope that) is always followed by the subjunctive. Quizais (perhaps) takes either the subjunctive or the indicative. Se cadra, very common in speech, also means “perhaps” and is used with the indicative.

Par souci de se démarquer de l'espagnol,: In an effort to stand apart from Spanish, some speakers wrongly “Galicianise” words that are identical in both languages: they add an i (*-eiro, *-eira) or change pl to pr. Para + infinitif personnel quand le suje: Para + personal infinitive when the subject of the purpose clause (ti) differs from that of the main clause.
Para mí introduit une opinion (« à mon a: Para mí introduces an opinion (“in my opinion”), whereas por mí means “as far as I'm concerned, I don't mind” or “because of me”. Para que est toujours suivi du subjoncti: Para que is always followed by the subjunctive.
Para que et a fin de que (plus formel) s: Para que and a fin de que (more formal) are always followed by the subjunctive. Participe + arren = bien que. arte = jus: Participle + arren = although. arte = until, gabe = without.
Participe + ezean signifie « à moins que: Participle + ezean means “unless, failing, if … not”. Baldin eta, placed before a condition with ba-, reinforces it (“provided that, if ever”).

Pas de « ne » explétif en basque : uste: No expletive “ne” in Basque: uste nuen baino = than I thought (French “que je ne pensais”).

Pensar se construit avec en : pensar en: Pensar takes en: pensar en algú.
Per a indique le destinataire, la destin: Per a indicates the recipient, the purpose of an object, a deadline and a point of view (per a mi). Perquè + subjonctif exprime le but (« po: Perquè + subjunctive expresses purpose (“so that”), whereas perquè + indicative expresses cause (“because”). Per tal que and a fi que, more formal, also require the subjunctive. If the subject is the same, per, per tal de or a fi de + infinitive is used.
Perquè exprimant le but est suivi du sub: Perquè expressing purpose is followed by the subjunctive: entenguis.
Perquè expressing purpose is followed by the subjunctive.
Perquè introduit une cause placée après: Perquè introduces a cause placed after the main clause. Com que (as) goes at the start of the sentence. Ja que (since) presents a cause the listener already knows. Don't confuse com que (cause) with com (how).
Perquè suivi de l'indicatif exprime la c: Perquè followed by the indicative expresses cause (because). Perquè followed by the subjunctive expresses purpose (so that). With the same subject, purpose is expressed by per a + infinitive. Don't confuse it with per què, in two words, which means “why”.
Personne ne sait avec certitude ce qui s: Nobody knows for sure what happened that night.

Piège fréquent : les formes tendrei ou s: Common trap: the forms tendrei or saldrei don't exist.
Piège pour francophones : « penser à que: Trap for French speakers: “to think about someone” (French “penser à”) is pensar en algú.

Plusieurs périphrases précisent le dérou: Several periphrases specify how the action unfolds: acabar de + infinitive (to have just), estar a punt de (to be about to), tornar a + infinitive (to do again, to start again), posar-se a (to start), deixar de (to stop), anar + gerund (gradual progression).
Plusieurs verbes demandent l'instrumenta: Several verbs take the instrumental -z where French uses “de” or “en”: gogoratu (to remember), jabetu (to realise), arduratu (to take care of), fidatu (to trust).
Plusieurs villes ont deux gentilés admis: Several cities have two accepted demonyms.

Pois, placé entre deux propositions, sig: Pois, placed between two clauses, means “because/for” and introduces an explanation: it is a false friend of French “puis” (then). Xa que and posto que present a known cause (since). Como, at the start of the sentence, introduces a cause stated before its consequence. Ponerse a + infinitif marque le début d': Ponerse a + infinitive marks the start of an action; echarse a is used mainly with reír and llorar for a sudden start. Ponerse a + infinitif signifie « se mett: Ponerse a + infinitive means “to start to”. Echarse a + infinitive is used for a sudden start, especially with reír, llorar, correr. Estar a punto de + infinitive means “to be about to” and, in the past, “to almost (do)”. Seguir + gerund means “to keep on, still”.

Por ende appartient à l'écrit soutenu ou: Por ende belongs to formal or legal writing.
Por mucho que + subjonctif pour un fait: Por mucho que + subjunctive for a fact presented as hypothetical.
Por muy + adjectif accordé + que + subjo: Por muy + agreeing adjective + que + subjunctive ; piso is masculine.

Pour adoucir une réalité pénible, le gal: To soften a painful reality, Galician uses euphemisms: finar or deixarnos for “to die”, pasar a mellor vida in a more solemn register. Irony often relies on antiphrasis and intonation: Boa a fixeches! means the exact opposite of what it says. This double-edged humour, retranca, is a Galician cultural trait.

Pour cesser ou recommencer : deixar de f: To stop or start again: deixar de fumar, volver a chamar.
Pour confirmer une action tout en introd: To confirm an action while adding a restriction, the participle is placed first and then picked up again with the auxiliary. With ere and negation, the same structure means “not even”.
Pour dire qu'une action est en train de: To say that an action is in progress, estar + gerund is used, like “to be doing” in English (French “être en train de”). The gerund ends in -ant (-ar verbs), -ent (-er and -re verbs) and -int (-ir verbs).
Pour dire sa profession ou son identité,: To state your profession or identity, Basque uses the article -a and not bat: “Irakaslea naiz”. Saying “irakasle bat naiz” copies the indefinite article of Spanish or French. bat stresses “one among others”, which doesn't fit here.
Pour dire « aller faire quelque chose »,: To say “to go and do something”, the verbal noun (-tze or -te) takes the allative -ra: erostera, afaltzera, ikustera. It is used with verbs of motion such as joan, etorri or irten.
Pour dire « bien que », on ajoute -(e)n: To say “although”, add -(e)n to the conjugated verb form, then arren. You can also put arren directly after the participle, without an auxiliary: this is the most common construction.
Pour donner un conseil avec « jo que tu: To give advice with “jo que tu” (“if I were you”), the conditional is used.
Pour donner une consigne polie à une per: To give a polite instruction to someone you address formally (vostede), use the 3rd person singular of the present subjunctive. In the plural (vostedes), use the 3rd person plural. The reflexive pronoun is attached to the end of the verb: séntese.
Pour exprimer un accident ou une action: To express an accident or an involuntary action, Catalan uses es + personal pronoun + verb: the thing concerned is the subject and the person is in the dative. Es + em gives se'm, es + li gives se li, es + ens gives se'ns. The verb agrees with the thing.
Pour exprimer une exception, on emploie: To express an exception, use llevat que or tret que (“unless”). For a condition, sempre que and a condició que (“provided that, on condition that”) and en cas que (“in case”). All these conjunctions require the subjunctive. Followed by the indicative, sempre que keeps its temporal meaning of “whenever”.
Pour exprimer « avoir beau » ou « si… qu: To express “however much” or “no matter how”, Valencian uses per molt que, per més que or per poc que followed by the subjunctive. The subjunctive is required whether the fact is real or hypothetical. A noun or adjective can be inserted, and it then agrees: per molts diners que tinga, per bo que siga.
Pour insister fortement sur un élément (: To strongly emphasise an element (“it is X who…”), use X + izan + a nominalised relative clause in -(e)na (or -(e)nak in the plural). The emphasised element stays in the absolutive, even if it is the subject of a transitive verb in the relative clause.
Pour l'an dernier, on dit « l'any passat: For last year, you say “l'any passat”, and for next year, “l'any que ve”.
Pour l'obligation ferme, on préfère have: For a firm obligation, haver de is preferred (he d'eixir, I have to go out).
Pour les verbes réguliers, il a la même: For regular verbs, it has the same form as the conjugated infinitive: cantar, cantares, cantarmos.
For regular verbs, it has the same form as the personal infinitive: falar, falares, falarmos.
Pour mettre en relief un moment, on util: To emphasise a point in time, the relative quan is used.
Pour mettre un complément en relief, on: To emphasise a complement, it is moved to the start or end of the sentence and picked up by a weak pronoun (el, la, li, en, hi, ho). This resumption is compulsory when the complement is dislocated. A partitive complement or one introduced by de is picked up by en.
Pour mettre un élément en relief (« c'es: To emphasise an element (“it is… that”), Spanish uses ser + element + the appropriate relative: donde for a place, cuando for a time, como for a manner, quien or el que for a person. The all-purpose “que” copied from French is to be avoided in careful language.
Pour mettre un élément en relief, on l'e: To emphasise an element, it is framed with ser and the appropriate relative: quen for a person, onde for a place, cando for a time, como for a manner. The verb ser is generally in the same tense as the main verb. The appropriate relative is preferred to a plain que copied from French “c'est ici que” (“it's here that”).

To emphasise an element, it is framed with ser and the appropriate relative: qui or el que for a person, on for a place, quan for a time, com for manner. Careful language avoids the all-purpose “que” copied from French (“és ací que”, “va ser aleshores que”).
Pour mettre un élément en relief, on uti: To emphasise an element, use “ser” + element + relative. For a person use “qui”, for a thing “el que”, for a place “on”. The order can also be reversed: relative clause first, emphasised element second.
Pour moi, c'est la meilleure option: For me, it's the best option
Pour parler de la mort, la langue soigné: To speak of death, careful language prefers zendu (to pass away) to hil, or the phrase “joan zaigu” (he has left us). People say adinekoak (the elderly) rather than zaharrak, and “gaixotasun luze baten ondorioz” (after a long illness) in death notices.

Pour présenter un incident comme involon: To present an incident as involuntary, Galician combines se and a dative pronoun (me, che, lle, nos, vos, lles): rompéuseme, queimóuselle. Pour rapporter des paroles, on emploie d: To report speech, use dir que, preguntar si or demanar que. If the introductory verb is in the past, the future becomes conditional and the present becomes imperfect. A reported order or request goes into the subjunctive: present after a present, imperfect (-ara) after a past.
Pour reprendre toute la proposition préc: To refer back to the whole previous clause (“which”, “what”), use lo que or, in a more formal register, lo cual. At the start of a sentence, to announce an idea (“what…, is…”), only lo que is possible.
To refer back to the whole previous clause, use lo cual (or lo que).
Pour reprendre toute une proposition («: To refer back to a whole clause (“which” after a comma), use la qual cosa or cosa que. For an unexpressed neutral antecedent (“what” at the start of a sentence), use allò que or el que. The form lo que is a Castilianism.
Pour reprendre toute une proposition, on: To refer back to a whole clause, use cosa que or la qual cosa.

Pour servir et valoir ce que de droit: For all legal intents and purposes
Pour situer un fait dans le passé (« il: To place an event in the past (“ago”), use fa + duration. For a situation that is still ongoing (“for/since”), say fa + duration + que + present, or des de fa + duration. Hi ha is not used in this sense.
To refer to a future moment: dentro de.
Pour structurer un texte argumentatif, o: To structure an argumentative text, formal phrases are available: pel que fa a and quant a (“as regards”), és a dir, a tall d'exemple, en definitiva. You write quant a and never “en quant a”.
Pour toute question, je reste à votre di: Should you have any questions, I remain at your disposal.
Pour traduire « ce que » et « ce qui »,: To translate “what” (French “ce que”, “ce qui”), Catalan uses “el que” or “allò que”. The form “lo que” is a Castilianism to avoid. “Tot el que” corresponds to “everything that”.
Pour tu, l'impératif des verbes en -ar s: For tu, the imperative of -ar verbs ends in -a: parla, mira, espera. For vosaltres, use the form in -eu (-ar, -er, -re verbs) or -iu (-ir verbs): parleu, beveu, dormiu. For vosté and vostés, use the present subjunctive: parle, parlen, passe, passen. Pour un lieu mis en relief, on emploie d: For an emphasised place, donde is used ; “que” is a Gallicism.
Pour un lieu mis en relief, on emploie l: For an emphasised place, the relative onde is used.

Pour un moment futur introduit par quan: For a future moment introduced by quan (when), the present subjunctive is used, not the future. This is a big difference from French, which says “quand tu arriveras” (literally “when you will arrive”). The same rule applies to tan prompte com (as soon as).
Pour un moment mis en relief, on emploie: For an emphasised time, cuando is used.
Pour un obstacle hypothétique, aínda que: For a hypothetical obstacle, aínda que requires the present subjunctive.
Pour une action antérieure, como si pren: For an earlier action, como si takes the pluperfect subjunctive.
Pour une action datée au passif, on empl: For a dated action in the passive, ser is used in the preterite.
Pour une action dont l'agent n'est pas p: For an action whose agent is not specified, use es + verb in the 3rd person. If the complement is a plural noun, the verb agrees with it (reflexive passive). With an intransitive verb or a clause, the verb stays singular (impersonal). This is the most natural way to translate French “on” (one/they/people) in ads, instructions and the press.
Pour une action involontaire, on emploie: For an involuntary action, use es + personal pronoun: se m'ha trencat.
Pour une action passée dans une période: For a past action in a period that isn't over yet (hui, este matí, esta setmana, enguany), the perfet is used: haver in the present + participle. For a finished period (ahir, la setmana passada, l'any passat), the passat perifràstic is normally used: vaig, vas, va, vam, vau, van + infinitive. The logic is the same as in Spanish between “he comido” and “comí”.
Pour une action ponctuelle et terminée d: For a one-off, completed action in the past, the periphrastic past is used.
Pour une action qui dure jusqu'au moment: For an action that continues up to the present, use levar + duration + gerund (or a + infinitive): levo tres anos vivindo aquí. Andar a + infinitive indicates a prolonged or repeated activity, often somewhat diffuse. Seguir + gerund marks continuation.
Pour une action sans agent précis, on em: For an action without a specific agent, use es + verb in the third person, like French “on”. The verb agrees with the following noun when it is plural: es lloga un pis, es lloguen pisos. This is the typical construction in ads and signs.
Pour une chose qu'on voit arriver : ir a: For something you can see coming: ir a + infinitive in the present.
Pour une concession au passé hypothétiqu: For a hypothetical concession in the past, the imperfect subjunctive is used: encara que plogués.
Pour une condition réelle, si est suivi: For a real condition, si is followed by the present indicative.
Pour une durée, on préfère « fa dos anys: For a duration, “fa dos anys que visc ací” is preferred to the calque “porte dos anys vivint ací”. Don't translate French “venir de” (to have just) as vindre de.
Pour une habitude, on garde l'indicatif: For a habit, the indicative is kept: “Quan arriba l'estiu, anem a la platja”.
Pour une hypothèse irréelle au présent (: For an unreal hypothesis in the present (“if I had, I would do”), the condition takes ba- + a hypothetical form: banu, bazenu, balu (ukan), banintz, bazina, balitz (izan). The result is in the conditional: erosiko nuke, joango nintzateke. With a periphrastic verb, the condition is formed on the future participle: etorriko balitz.
Pour une hypothèse non réalisée dans le: For an unfulfilled hypothesis in the past, use se + compound pluperfect subjunctive (houbese + participle) or, very often, the simple imperfect subjunctive, with the context indicating the past. In the main clause, you find the simple conditional, the compound conditional (habería + participle) or, in careful language, the -ra form. As in French, the conditional is never used after se.

For an unfulfilled hypothesis in the past, use si + pluperfect subjunctive, and the main clause goes into the conditional perfect (habría + participle) or, very often, the pluperfect subjunctive. After si, the conditional is impossible. If the consequence concerns the present, the main clause is in the simple conditional.

For an unfulfilled hypothesis in the past, put the pluperfect subjunctive after si and the conditional perfect (hauria + participle) in the main clause. Valencian only uses the auxiliary haver, even with verbs that take “être” in French (venir, partir, aller, arriver).
Pour une hypothèse peu probable ou irrée: For an unlikely or unreal hypothesis in the present, use si + imperfect subjunctive (in -ara, -era, -ira in Valencian) and the conditional in the main clause. The conditional never appears after si. Where French uses an imperfect indicative, Valencian uses an imperfect subjunctive.
Pour une hypothèse, si est suivi du subj: For a hypothesis, si is followed by the imperfect subjunctive, never the conditional.
Pour une personne, on emploie en général: For a person, the stressed pronoun is generally used: pense en ella.
Pour une personne, on emploie plutôt la: For a person, the stressed form is preferred: parlàvem d'ell.
Pour une personne, on emploie plutôt le: For a person, the strong pronoun is preferred: penso en ella.

Pour une situation qui dure, on dit fa +: For an ongoing situation, you say fa + duration + que + present.
Pour une supposition sur le passé, on em: For an assumption about the past, the conditional is used.
Pour une supposition sur le présent, le: For an assumption about the present, the conditional would be a mistake.
Pour vouvoyer avec usted ou ustedes, l'i: To address people formally with usted or ustedes, the imperative uses the present subjunctive forms: hable, hablen, coma, coman, escriba, escriban. Verbs that are irregular in the 1st person keep that irregularity: vengo gives venga, hago gives haga, digo gives diga. A few forms must be memorised: vaya, sea, esté, dé. Pronouns are attached to the end of the affirmative verb.
Pour « aussi … que », on place bezain en: For “as … as”, bezain goes between the element compared and the adjective: zu bezain altua. For “as much as” with a verb or a quantity, use bezainbeste, and the element compared takes the same case as the subject (nik bezainbeste). “Not so …” is ez … hain.
Pour « constipé » au sens digestif, on d: For “constipated” in the digestive sense, you say “restret”.

Pour « je suis allé » (action terminée),: For “I went” (completed action), you say joan nintzen.
Pour « pendant que », on ajoute bitartea: For “while”, add bitartean to the verb conjugated in -(e)n. For “until”, put arte after the participle. For “since”, add -tik to the verb conjugated in -(e)n: -(e)netik.
Pour « pouvoir » avec un verbe intransit: For “can” with an intransitive verb, use the verb stem followed by naiteke, zaitezke, daiteke, gaitezke, zaitezkete, daitezke. The stem is the participle without -tu or -i: sartu gives sar, etorri gives etor, gertatu gives gerta.
Pour « se rendre compte », on dit decata: For “to realise”, you say decatarse de or darse conta de.
Pour « si j'avais fait, j'aurais fait »,: For “if I had done, I would have done”, the subordinate clause takes the participle (often followed by izan) + the hypothetical form in ba- ; the main clause combines the future participle in -ko and the auxiliary in the past (zuen, nuen, genuen).
Pour « si j'avais, si j'étais », on empl: For “if I had, if I were”, use ba- + hypothetical form: banu, bazenu, balu (ukan), banintz, bazina, balitz (izan). The main clause is in the conditional in -ke: nuke, luke, nintzateke, litzateke, often preceded by the future participle in -ko.

Quand l'antécédent est indéterminé, rech: When the antecedent is indefinite, sought after or non-existent, the verb in the relative clause goes into the subjunctive. If the antecedent is known and real, the indicative is used.

Quand l'objet donné, dit ou envoyé est p: When the object given, said or sent is plural, the NOR-NORI-NORK auxiliary takes -zki-: dizkiot (I … them to him), dizkizut (I … them to you), dizkidazu (you … them to me), dizkiet (I … them to them), dizkiegu (we … them to them).
Quand l'ordre a un destinataire (« donne: When the order has a recipient (“give me, tell him”), use the participle + iezadazu (to me), iezaiozu (to him/her), iezaguzu (to us). Some verbs have very common synthetic forms: emadazu, esaiozu.
